The test image shows a mango leaf with brown/necrotic lesions concentrated at the tip and upper edges, with some irregular brown spots on the leaf surface. The damage appears as dead tissue at the leaf apex/tip area, with the rest of the leaf remaining green.

Key features:
- Tip necrosis / dieback from the apex
- Brown dry lesions at the tip and upper portion
- Rest of leaf is green and intact
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No black sooty coating (rules out Sooty_Mould)
- Candidates: Die_Back or Anthracnose

Now let me view one reference image from Die_Back to compare:

The Die_Back reference shows a fully desiccated, entirely brown/dead leaf with severe whole-leaf necrosis. The test image is quite different — it has a mostly green leaf with necrotic lesions concentrated at the tip and scattered irregular brown spots on the blade. This pattern (tip lesions + discrete spots on green tissue) is more characteristic of Anthracnose, which causes dark brown irregular lesions that can start at leaf tips and margins with spots distributed across the blade.
